newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker amid soft U.S., new supply.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker amid soft U.S., new supply.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed softer in quiet trade on Monday, amid weakness in U.S. treasuries, the weight of new supply and some selling by Japanese investors overnight, dealers and analysts said.

"The market was technically overbought from Friday, and in Canada there was the long Ontario deal," said Philip Strathy, chief investment officer with Strathy Investments Ltd. "I think the flows were light."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.32 to C$113.96 to yield 6.892 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 19/32 to yield 6.83 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from 10 basis points at Friday's close.
"It was a pretty non-eventful day. We followed the U.S. market down," said one bond dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "I think it was more so some Japanese selling last night."

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied sharply on Friday as traders scrambled to cover short positions. With those short positions covered, there was little new buying entering the market, analysts said.

New supply in the Canadian market also affected prices, dealers said. The province of Ontario this morning set C$500 million of 7.6 percent bonds due June 2, 2027 in financial markets. The offering was a reopening of a previous issue.

The bond was priced at C$106.544 to yield 7.071 percent, 20.5 basis points over the Government of Canada 8.0 percent bond due June, 2023. The bonds will pay interest on December 2 and June 2. The issue will be delivered on June 16.
Canadian housing starts and capacity utilization data this morning were largely in line with expectations and had little impact on the bond market, analysts said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.34 to C$106.23 to yield 6.395 percent, while the U.S. 10-year fell 13/32 to 6.55 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 16 basis points from 14 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.90 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.04 percent.
